wikidata.note: Confirmed by the agent from the Wikidata item: description 'mountain range in the Dolomites', coordinates 46.6186, 12.3056 match the place; a person should re-check.

draw.note: The tourism board calls the Three Peaks 'the icon of the Dolomites', a headline of the UNESCO World Heritage Site (official_highlight); the toll road needs a booked slot and the car park fills before 07:00 in summer.

standing.note: The defining walk of the Sexten and Ampezzo Dolomites.

distinction.note: No other walk in Italy circles a group of north faces like these.

easy_payoff.note: From Rifugio Auronzo the towers are seen from the side; the classic north-face view needs about an hour to Forcella Lavaredo.

weather.note: Still worth walking in cloud, but the north-face view is the payoff.

records.why: A loop round the three towers whose north faces are the image of the Dolomites.

v.note: Toll road to Rifugio Auronzo: online booking only, 40 EUR per car, ticket valid 12 h; or shuttle 444 from Dobbiaco

access_cost.note: From the municipality's parking page.

v.name: Three Peaks, a highlight of the UNESCO World Heritage Site (3 Zinnen tourism board)

records.unique_because: Three 500 m north faces seen all the way round on a walkers' path

pairs_with.reason: The Cadini viewpoint path leaves from Rifugio Auronzo, the loop's start: a short add-on

wikidata.note: Confirmed by the agent from the Wikidata item: description 'mountain range in the Dolomites (the Cadini group the viewpoint faces)', coordinates 46.5793, 12.2873 match the place; a person should re-check.

draw.note: Reached on the same booked toll road as the Tre Cime loop and done as its add-on; inside the UNESCO Dolomites (inherited designation, not draw). Widely photographed, but visitors come for the Tre Cime first.

standing.note: The most dramatic spire view in the Misurina area.

records.standing_scope: Misurina and the Tre Cime toll road

distinction.note: Spire panoramas of this kind exist (Seceda, 60 km), but none of the Cadini.

easy_payoff.note: The view is only at the end of the exposed spur.

weather.note: A view of spires; in cloud there is nothing to see.

records.why: A short spur to a rocky promontory facing the jagged Cadini di Misurina spires.

v.note: Same Rifugio Auronzo toll road and booking as the Tre Cime loop

designations.note: Inherited from the Dolomites serial site as for the Tre Cime; not confirmed on a land-manager page for this spot.

wikidata.note: Confirmed by the agent from the Wikidata item: description 'lake in the Dolomites, Northern Italy', coordinates 46.5204, 12.2236 match the place; a person should re-check.

draw.note: The turquoise lake under the Sorapiss is a destination in itself: the 20-car Passo Tre Croci car park fills by 06:00-06:30 in July (sells out early). No designation of its own; inside the UNESCO Dolomites (inherited).

standing.note: The best-known hike-in lake around Cortina.

distinction.note: Other hike-in lakes lie within 20 km (Federa, Limides) but none with this colour.

easy_payoff.note: The lake is only at the end of the 6 km traverse.

weather.note: The colour needs sun; the walk works in cloud.

records.why: A milky-turquoise lake under the Sorapiss wall at the end of a cliff-side path.

access_cost.note: No booking or toll; the constraint is the small car park.

designations.note: Inherited; not confirmed on a land-manager page.

wikidata.note: Confirmed by the agent from the Wikidata item: description 'mountain in the Dolomites', coordinates 46.5093, 12.054 match the place; a person should re-check.

standing.note: The most accessible of the Ampezzo WWI open-air museums.

distinction.note: Lagazuoi (5 km) and Monte Piana (30 km) are the same kind.

easy_payoff.note: The chairlift lands next to the trenches.

weather.note: Trenches and towers work in cloud; the panorama does not.

records.why: Restored WWI trenches and gun posts among five rock towers, a chairlift ride from the road.

access_cost.note: The chairlift is optional; a path climbs from Bai de Dones.
